ticket.title: invocation spans never record task_key, so a task cost cannot be answered from spans alone
ticket.description:
Measured 2026-11-10 in the live suite log: 898 spans, zero of them carry task_key, and the fields present are binary, branch, command, duration_ms, repo, span_id, started_at_ms, status, trace_id. Nothing is wrong with the writing path - the field exists on TelemetrySpan and InvocationSpan simply never sets it, so no producer anywhere in the tree populates it. GB-339 acceptance says a task cost is answerable from spans alone, and today it is not: a span says which binary ran in which repository on which branch, and nothing joins it to the ticket whose work it was. The join key exists and is cheap - storypole already knows the active claim at process start, and claim carries the task key - so this is a producer change rather than a schema one. Wanted: InvocationSpan resolves the claimed task key for the current repository at start, records it, and stays absent when no claim is held (absent is honest: an unclaimed run is not attributable). Acceptance: a span emitted while a task is claimed carries its key, a span emitted with no claim carries none, and a query over the log can total duration per task_key.

PARTIAL 2026-11-10 (common 07eed3b): the mechanism exists, the wiring does not, and the acceptance as written needs a decision. Landed: InvocationSpan::start_for_task(binary, command, task_key), sharing one builder with start so the emission policy and id rules cannot diverge. Why caller-supplied rather than resolved, measured rather than assumed: (1) the suite records 217 claims and the sampled ones carry branch None - worktree branch matching has nothing to match; (2) two agents can hold claims in one suite concurrently, so there is no single ambient answer; (3) gaugeblock-workspace cannot read the claims without depending on storypole-core, which inverts the dependency graph, or parsing ticket records, which GaugeblockPaths::storypole_tickets explicitly says to read through storypole. Two things remain and the first is a decision: how a tool learns which ticket it is working on - a flag, an environment variable storypole exports when it spawns a tool, or a claim-marker file written per worktree - and then wiring each tool. GB-339 acceptance should be reworded either way, because task cost answerable from spans alone is only true for tools that were told, and a tool that guesses would poison the corpus. Not test-observed: the emission policy refuses to write from a cargo test binary (BW-33) and a test that defeated it would write into the real suite log, so the assignment is covered by compilation and its policy path by the guard tests.

DECIDED 2026-11-10: environment variable (option B), with three rules that refuse rather than guess. The owner chose B and raised the risk that matters - a leftover or incorrect variable attributing work to the wrong task - and that risk shaped the design rather than being noted after it.

THE MECHANISM. GAUGEBLOCK_TASK_KEY plus GAUGEBLOCK_TASK_EXPIRES_MS, read once at span open (gaugeblock_workspace task_keys, common 223de77). Chosen exactly the way GAUGEBLOCK_TRACE_ID was chosen: a parent that knows the fact hands it to the child it spawns, and the child needs no flag, no store access and no knowledge of storypole. A flag cannot reach an MCP server, which has no per-call argv; a claim marker file would be a third copy of what the store already holds, which is the mistake that cost GB-347 and GB-349 in one session.

THE THREE RULES, all refusing rather than guessing, because a wrong task_key is worse than an absent one: (1) the key must come with a lease that has not expired - one millisecond past is refused, and an expiring-now lease is refused, because the variable has outlived the claim that justified it; (2) PREFIX-NUMBER only; (3) the prefix must be this repository own or the suite harness prefix, so MTR-9 in storypole is refused while GB-305 in storypole is allowed, because harness work happens in members constantly. A refused key records nothing and says why on stderr - a silent refusal is indistinguishable from a broken emitter.

WHY THE EXPIRY IS REQUIRED, not optional: the leftover case the owner named is precisely `export GAUGEBLOCK_TASK_KEY=GB-355` with nothing bounding it. Making the lease optional would leave that case unbounded rather than merely likely.

PROVEN LIVE, because the environment path is the one a unit test cannot reach (set_var is unsafe in edition 2024): fresh lease -> span records task_key=GB-356; expired lease, no lease, and MTR-9 inside storypole -> no key plus the reason on stderr; GB-305 inside storypole -> recorded. Nine unit tests cover the pure verdict at every boundary; the judgement is split from the environment read for exactly that reason.

WIRED SO FAR: storypole verify (cba65ea) hands the claim to every process in the chain - fmt, clippy, nextest, docs and whatever they spawn - bounding it by the claim lease when one is held and a window from now otherwise. That is the coverage GB-339 wanted, since a task cost is mostly the tools it spawned.

REMAINING, and the acceptance rewording: (a) outfeed gate is the obvious next exporter, since it already exports TRACE_ENV at execute.rs:75; (b) long-lived processes must opt out or re-read per request - the benchwork daemon inheriting a launch-time key would credit a day of work to one ticket, and that policy belongs beside the daemon, which is GB-293 territory; (c) GB-339 acceptance should say attributable work rather than cost answerable from spans alone, because it is only true for tools that were told, and unattributed time should be reported separately rather than folded into a guess.
